thread:
Sam B: Quick sync — we need to decide who owns SLO->routing mappings for Hosted/Dedicated/Private and how we deprecate the old `route_selector` behavior. Planning a deprecation in Q2. Thoughts?
Julia K: Agree we can't leave ambiguity. Currently product sets SLOs but infra handles routing keys. That's a collision.
Mike L: +1. Practical ask: who ships the fallback semantics? e.g., if Dedicated runs out of capacity, which model variant do we route to and who authorizes it?
Devon R: My vote is infra owns the runtime fallback policy (safe defaults), product owns the mapping from SLOs to high-level intents. Keep a clear separation: intent vs enforcement.
Anya P: That split works. Product defines intents like `low_cost`, `low_latency`, `private_only`; infra translates to concrete routes and fallbacks. We need an audit header when infra overrides intent.
Sam B: Good. Need to codify in a small RFC + a migration plan. Also want to deprecate `route_selector` (legacy) in favor of `intent_policy`. 12-week deprecation window?
Mike L: 12 weeks sounds fair if we provide a migration CLI and console notices. Also need a per-tenant feature flag to opt-in early and a runtime toggle for canary.
Julia K: Can we map responsibilities: Product -> `intent_policy` schema, onboarding docs, examples. Infra -> runtime enforcement, telemetry keys, `X-Route-Fallback` header, and rollout mechanics.
Devon R: Ops/Reliability should own SLO enforcement tooling + alerts tied to routing changes. We should also add a metric: `route.fallback.count` with tags {from_env,to_env,intent}.
Mike L: Example intent snippet for the migration guide:
```
intent_policy:
  name: low_latency
  prefer: [hosted-v2, dedicated-gpu]
  fallback: [dedicated-cpu, private-quantized]
  tolerances:
    latency_ms: 150
    p99: 300
```
Keep it simple.
Anya P: Also need a clear billing/commit note: Dedicated commitments shouldn't be silently bypassed by fallbacks unless customer allows it. Add `allow_dedicated_bypass: false` default at tenant level.
Sam B: Good call. So deprecation checklist: (1) Publish RFC and schema, (2) Console + API warnings for 12 weeks, (3) Migration CLI + examples, (4) Per-tenant opt-in flags, (5) Canary rollout (5% -> 25% -> 100%), (6) Disable legacy after window.
Julia K: For telemetry mapping: legacy `route_selector` emitted `route.selected` only. New flow must emit `intent.requested`, `route.selected`, `route.fallback_reason`. That will help quality regressions.
Devon R: Also we should include a short-lived compatibility layer: translate `route_selector` to an inferred `intent_policy` server-side and emit a warning event. That eases client migration.
Mike L: Ops: can we add an automated evaluation job that runs prompts through both routes and diffs outputs during canary? We should gate promotion on quality regressions <= threshold.
Anya P: Yes — Redwood Optimize can run that under `migration-eval` workspace. We need to surface regressed prompts in console.
Sam B: Who wants to own the RFC doc and migration tickets? I can draft RFC with proposed schema. Need infra owner for enforcement/runtime: @Devon R?
Devon R: I'll take runtime enforcement and the compatibility shim ticket. Will coordinate with Mike for metrics and canary infra.
deploy-bot: deploy:canary started for route-intent-flag v1 -> 5% traffic (initiated by Devon R) :rocket:
Mike L: I'll own the migration CLI + canary evaluation harness.
Julia K: I'll update onboarding docs and product examples. I'll also draft messaging for customers with Dedicated commits.
Sam B: Perfect. I'll open the RFC PR today and tag all of you. Thanks — let's aim to have canary infra ready in 3 weeks.
Anya P: Quick follow-up: please ensure the header with fallback reason is kept for at least 90 days for audits.
Devon R: noted, will add retention config.
Sam B: end of thread — RFC PR link will go in this thread when ready.
